items.snippet: As we've seen with the Ubuntu critical CVE-2026-98432 (CVSS 9.8), AI-dicovered zero day exploit are being reported at an exponential rate and we don't have the process for dealing with the flood of exploits in real time. What we need is an AI-based system for autopatching systems based on real time information. The vendor's fix can take days or weeks to be out (is the Ubuntu thing patched yet?) and meanwhile the grid is vulnerable to exploitation, especially AI worms. Repairer is a small program that runs on each of your servers. The day an exploit goes public it puts up a stopgap that blocks it, and once the real fix is up it takes the stopgap back off by itself. A stopgap only takes something away — drop certain packets, turn off a kernel module or service, remove a setuid bit. It never opens a port, installs or downloads anything, nor runs code. It arms an undo playbook before applying the stopgap, so the change reverts if affects any services. It only ever acts on rules you sign with a (hardware) crypto wallet. items.title: Price pressures persisted in October
items.snippet: Data: Bureau of Labor Statistics ; Chart: Courtenay Brown/Axios Inflation remained hot in October, according to data from the Labor Department released on Tuesday. Why it matters: The Consumer Price Index shows that even as gasoline prices steadied, inflation pressures elsewhere remained stubborn. By the numbers: CPI rose 0.4% last month, slowing from the 0.6% increase in September. Gasoline prices gained 1% in October, a sharp slowdown from the 9.1% surge in September, the Labor Department said. Core CPI, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, advanced 0.3% for the third straight month, with higher prices for recreation, medical care, car insurance and airline fares contributing to the increase. Of note: The Labor Department did not publish year-over-year inflation rates for October. Last year's government shutdown left a gap in the data that prevents direct comparisons with October 2025. But if one assumes the October 2025 readings were halfway between September and November, year-over-year inflation comes to 4% — or 2.8% excluding food and energy. items.title: The AI industry's week from hell
items.snippet: A week of political upheaval , financial turmoil and salacious scandal delivered one final indignity to the AI industry Tuesday, as Anthropic's staggering IPO target fell short of expectations. Why it matters: The bubble is wobbling. Investors, businesses and governments need a spectacular success from Anthropic to stave off a crisis of confidence that could tear through the broader economy. Facing new political headwinds, the industry can scarcely afford another setback — much less the spectacle of AI's crown jewel losing its luster on Wall Street. Zoom in: Anthropic announced plans Tuesday to raise as much as $64.4 billion in one of the largest IPOs in history, targeting a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion. That's roughly $600 billion below what investors envisioned just months ago, as slowing revenue growth, soaring infrastructure costs and a punishing market selloff tempered expectations. Anthropic's annualized revenue reached $81 billion in October, but its long-term commitments to chips, data centers and computing infrastructure have also climbed to nearly $901 billion. How Much Is Anthropic Really Worth?
items.snippet: While investors digest the news of Nvidia boss Jensen Huang’s exit and its implications on the AI build-out , they are simultaneously mulling another nebulous question: How much is Anthropic worth? If everything goes according to plan, the market should give its answer when the company debuts on the Nasdaq exchange next week. Anthropic has set a tentative pricing range of between $1.25 trillion and $1.4 trillion, but several investors we spoke to expect it to price above that range. Pricing an initial public offering above the proposed range “is a signal of underlying demand momentum, which is very important to get people excited to participate,” said Samantha Lau, chief investment officer of small- and mid-cap growth equities at AllianceBernstein.

items.title: Jensen Huang's implosion at Nvidia leaves trail of collateral damage
items.snippet: Jensen Huang's self-destruction has left a trail of collateral damage that threatens to ensnare the board of Nvidia and the AI boom itself . Why it matters: Huang was a singular leader in the global economy, capable of exciting or calming markets with a single sentence and viewed as a virtually indestructible force behind Nvidia's rise. The big picture: His sudden exit after reports of multiple affairs — one with a suspected Chinese spy and the other with a direct report — has wiped out more than $600 billion in value from Nvidia's market cap. "His visionary leadership is going to be missed — it's not going to be replaced," Joel Shulman, CEO of ERShares, which has owned Nvidia shares since 2005, tells Axios. Zoom in: With the uncertainty over Huang's tenure at Nvidia now resolved, the attention will quickly pivot to a slew of unanswered questions, including: What will the investigations uncover? Just because he's gone doesn't mean this is over. If the FBI probe or the independent investigation ordered by the board show that Huang gave favorable treatment to Megaspeed — the company led by the suspected spy Alice Huang — he and Nvidia could face serious consequences. Show HN: MergeMax, a monthly ranking of public merged PRs on GitHub
items.snippet: Hi HN, the main idea around MergeMax is that the user can look themselves up and compare themselves against all the other people on the board. No sign-in required. We currently support monthly and daily leaderboards. I built MergeMax since I kept seeing people post on X about @poteto's merge count and I knew I could probably create something to easily see her and other popular dev's GitHub public PRs. I quickly found out however that her PRs aren't visible via our methods, since most of her PRs are private/not on GitHub. I also wanted to create a place where people can easily see the amount of merges top accounts do each month, now that agents have the ability to create thousands of PRs themselves. Currently we only support public PRs as well as the contribution total that gets provided by GitHub directly: - A public PR only counts if it's public, merged, and authored by the account that's being looked up, and merged within the specified period. - I use GitHub's search API for PR counts. items.title: How the Microsoft outage impacted courts and governments
items.snippet: Courts and governments worldwide felt the impact of this week's Microsoft outage, which sidelined work and stymied communication. Why it matters: When Microsoft's popular workplace software went offline Thursday, it meant an extended lunch break for some offices — but for the courts and governments, it raised questions about the vulnerabilities of the technology underpinning justice and governance. Case in point: The state of Maine's judicial branch warned in a Thursday alert that requests for protection orders filed by email — urgent requests to keep parties safe from harm — may not have been received. Multiple court documents reviewed by Axios show lawyers requesting deadline extensions or alerting judges to the outage impacting their work. That includes DOJ lawyers: Government attorneys asked for an extension in the case brought by Rep. Joyce Beatty (D-Ohio) over President Trump 's Kennedy Center takeover , saying the outage prevented them from "completing the necessary coordination." items.title: Inside the aftermath of the Logan Circle shooting
items.snippet: It took just minutes for a gunman to shoot six people and upend one of D.C.'s busiest neighborhoods. The big picture: Thursday morning's violence left one person dead in a Logan Circle gym and five others injured nearby. The gunman later shot himself, police said. The massive police response shut down streets, sent nearly a dozen schools into lockdown and forced residents to shelter in place. By evening, the streets around VIDA Fitness, where the shooting began, were quiet. Several nearby businesses remained closed, with police tape blocking off storefronts and officers standing watch. Councilmember Brooke Pinto held a vigil . People left flowers and notes outside of the VIDA . "Logan Circle is still a place for love," read one. "VIDA, you are and will continue to be a safe haven for many," read another. But life also carried on: A delivery van unloaded Christmas trees at Whole Foods, and 14th Street bars put out signs advertising happy hour. Flowers and handwritten notes line the outside of VIDA Fitness. Photo: Mimi Montgomery/Axios One note reads: "VIDA, you are and will continue to be a safe haven for many." items.title: FAA back at "full operations" after Friday outage, Transportation Sec. says
items.snippet: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Saturday that all FAA systems are back to "full operations" after an hours-long outage Friday evening that grounded all air traffic across the U.S. The big picture: Duffy reiterated his plea to Congress to fund upgrades to the nation's air traffic control equipment, explaining that proper upgrades could have prevented the ground stop. Driving the news: Duffy explained that the outage was caused when a contractor performed routine maintenance on a telecommunications line to upgrade a copper wire to fiber-optic cable and install a new router. "It was such an old wire that it was being discontinued, meaning that line was going to get shut down. So we had to switch it over from old copper," Duffy said. Duffy said it's unclear whether the outage occurred because of contractor error or faulty equipment, but they are working to figure that out. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford warned that up to 5,000 flight cancellations will remain throughout today, but airlines have assured the agency that they should return to normal operations by the end of the day Sunday.
